mainTopic: The end of the aggadah about how long 'soon' is for הקב"ה, and then a new משנה about a forced גט (גט מעושה): when pressure on the husband makes the גט valid, invalid, or only partly valid.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an aggadah: רב אחא בר יעקב learns that 'soon' for הקב"ה can mean 852 years. Then a new משנה teaches that a גט forced by a Jewish בית דין is כשר, but a גט forced by gentiles is פסול, unless the gentiles are only enforcing what the Jewish court ordered. רב נחמן quoting שמואל gives four cases, depending on who forced the husband and whether the forcing was lawful (כדין). One of them is the middle result 'פסול ופוסל': the גט is invalid, but it still forbids the woman to a כהן. The גמרא asks how gentile force can produce that middle result. רב משרשיא's answer, that the גט is valid by Torah law, is rejected as a mistake. Instead, the lawful gentile case is made פוסל only because people could confuse it with a lawful Jewish-forced גט. Next, אביי asks רב יוסף how unordained judges in בבל can force a גט at all. רב יוסף answers that they act as agents of the ordained judges, but only in common matters. Finally, a new משנה teaches that a town rumor can establish קידושין or גירושין unless there is an אמתלא. The גמרא starts rereading the משנה to fit רב אשי's rule that rumors after נישואין are ignored, and this reading continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How long is 'soon' for God?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב concludes from the earlier discussion that 'soon' (מהרה) for הקב"ה means 852 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: We can learn from this that 'soon' for the Master of the World is 852 years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an aggadic discussion from just before this point. רב אחא בר יעקב draws a lesson from the number 852.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק warns that if the people sin they 'will soon perish'. Their time in the land was linked to the number 852. So רב אחא בר יעקב reasons that God's 'soon' can be a very long time by human standards.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a formula for drawing a conclusion)
Soon, quickly
The Master of the World, meaning הקב"ה

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Learn from this: the 'soon' of the Master of the World
is eight hundred and fifty-two years.
phrases.notes: He is reading the word 'soon' in the פסוק 'you will soon perish' (דברים 4:26).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the aggadic discussion from the previous part of the daf.

steps.title: A forced divorce document: Jewish court versus gentiles
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a גט מעושה forced by Jews is כשר, but one forced by gentiles is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A גט that the husband was forced to give is valid if Jews forced him, but invalid if gentiles forced him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a husband who was pressured into giving a גט, and asks whether that גט works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גט must be given willingly. Even so, the משנה says pressure from a Jewish בית דין does not ruin the גט, while pressure from gentiles does. So the key question is who is doing the forcing.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A forced גט, given by a husband under pressure
Valid
Invalid

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A forced bill of divorce: if forced by Jews, it is valid,
and if forced by gentiles, it is invalid.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט forced by a Jewish court is valid; a גט forced by gentiles is invalid.

steps.title: Gentiles may pressure the husband on the Jewish court's orders
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that gentiles may beat the husband if they tell him to do what the Jews say, and then the גט is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with gentiles: they may beat him and say to him, 'Do what the Jews are telling you,' and the גט is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an exception to the rule it just gave about gentiles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the gentiles are not the real source of the pressure. They are only enforcing the Jewish court's decision. Because the husband is told to obey the Jews, it counts as Jewish pressure, and the גט is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: They beat (him)
Do what the Jews are telling you

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict the previous line. Gentiles forcing a גט on their own makes it פסול. Gentiles acting as the enforcers of a Jewish בית דין is a different case.

phrases.english: But with gentiles, they may beat him
and say to him:
'Do what the Jews are telling you,'
(and it is valid).
phrases.notes: Some versions of the משנה have these words in round brackets and some don't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the rule that a גט forced by gentiles is invalid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gentiles may pressure the husband on behalf of the Jewish court, and the גט is valid.

steps.title: שמואל: a Jewish court forcing lawfully or unlawfully
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: if a Jewish court forced the גט lawfully, it is כשר. If it forced it unlawfully, the גט is פסול but still פוסל.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: A גט forced by Jews, if done lawfully, is valid. If done unlawfully, it is invalid, but it still disqualifies her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. שמואל adds a second question: was the forcing done according to the law?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's 'valid' case only applies when the husband really was required by law to divorce. If the court forced him without a legal basis, the גט does not work. Even so, it leaves a mark: it is 'פוסל', meaning it disqualifies the woman from marrying a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Lawfully, when the הלכה requires the divorce
Unlawfully, without a legal basis
Disqualifies (her from marrying a כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: 'פסול' does not mean the גט has no effect at all. It cannot end the marriage, but it still forbids her to a כהן.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
A bill of divorce forced by Jews:
if done lawfully, it is valid;
if done unlawfully, it is invalid, but it disqualifies.
phrases.notes: It disqualifies the woman from marrying a כהן, even though she is still married.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: גֵּט הַמְעוּשֶּׂה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and refines the משנה's ruling about a Jewish court.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jewish court forcing lawfully: כשר. Forcing unlawfully: פסול ופוסל.

steps.title: שמואל: gentiles forcing lawfully or unlawfully
steps.stepSummary: If gentiles forced the גט lawfully, it is פסול ופוסל. If they forced it unlawfully, it is not a גט at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: With gentiles: if done lawfully, it is invalid but disqualifies. If done unlawfully, it does not have even the scent of a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל completes his four cases by discussing gentiles who force the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the law required the divorce, gentile pressure makes the גט invalid, though it still disqualifies her from a כהן. When there was no legal basis at all, the paper means nothing and she is not disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'scent' of a גט, meaning even a trace of a divorce's effect

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's four levels are: Jews lawfully = כשר. Jews unlawfully = פסול ופוסל. Gentiles lawfully = פסול ופוסל. Gentiles unlawfully = not even the scent of a גט.

phrases.english: And by gentiles: if done lawfully, it is invalid and disqualifies;
if done unlawfully,
it does not have even the scent of a bill of divorce.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gentiles forcing lawfully: פסול ופוסל. Gentiles forcing unlawfully: no effect at all.

steps.title: Either gentiles can force a גט or they cannot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the ruling that a גט forced by gentiles lawfully is פסול ופוסל. If gentile force counts, the גט should be fully כשר. If it does not count, the גט should not even be פוסל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it, there is a problem. If gentiles are able to force a גט, it should be fully valid. If they are not able to, it should not even disqualify her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling from step 5 that a גט forced lawfully by gentiles is פסול ופוסל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא sets up two options. Either gentile force works, and then the גט should be כשר, or it does not work, and then it should have no effect at all. A middle result, פסול ופוסל, seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it; both options lead to a problem
People whose forcing counts legally
The גט is not valid, but it still disqualifies the woman from marrying a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: פוסל here does not mean the woman may remarry. It means she is not divorced, but she is still forbidden to a כהן, as if she were a divorcee.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it, there is a problem!
If gentiles are people whose forcing counts,
then it should also be fully valid!
If they are not people whose forcing counts,
then it should not disqualify her either!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic of the middle category in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a גט forced lawfully by gentiles is פסול ופוסל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-option dilemma: gentile force either counts or it does not, so the גט should be fully כשר or have no effect, not something in between.

steps.title: By Torah law the גט is valid, but the רבנן made it invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא says that by Torah law a גט forced by gentiles is כשר. The רבנן called it פסול so that women would not run to gentiles to force their husbands and free themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: By Torah law, a גט forced by gentiles is valid. Why did the רבנן say it is invalid? So that not every woman would go and rely on a gentile to free herself from her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא answers the dilemma: gentile force really does count, and the invalidity is only a rule of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the middle result. Because by Torah law the גט works, it is פוסל her from a כהן. Because the רבנן added a rule against it, she still cannot remarry. That gives פסול ופוסל.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law, as opposed to a rule of the רבנן
Relies on someone else to get what she wants
Frees herself, gets out of the marriage

phrases.english: רב משרשיא said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה – גֵּט מְעוּשֶּׂה בַּגּוֹיִם, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: By Torah law, a גט forced by gentiles is valid.
And why did they say it is invalid?
So that not each and every woman
would go and rely on a gentile,
and free herself from her husband's hand.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits Torah law from a rule of the רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed gentile force must either fully work or fully fail.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law it works, which makes her פסולה to a כהן; the רבנן made it invalid, so she cannot remarry.

steps.title: Then why does an unlawful gentile-forced גט have no effect at all?
steps.stepSummary: If gentile force counts by Torah law, then a גט forced by gentiles unlawfully should be like one forced unlawfully by Jews, which is פסול ופוסל. Yet שמואל said it has not even the smell of a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why is it that when gentiles forced it unlawfully there is not even the smell of a גט? It should be like Jews forcing unlawfully, and it should also disqualify her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב משרשיא's answer by comparing it to שמואל's ruling about gentiles forcing unlawfully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב משרשיא treats gentile force like Jewish force by Torah law. But in step 4, Jews forcing unlawfully gives פסול ופוסל, while in step 5, gentiles forcing unlawfully gives nothing at all. If the two were equal, both should be פסול ופוסל.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what you said is true
Unlawfully; forcing a man who did not have to divorce
The smell of a גט; even a slight effect of a divorce

phrases.english: If so, when it was forced unlawfully,
why does it not have even the smell of a גט?!
Let unlawful forcing by gentiles be like unlawful forcing by Jews,
phrases.notes: Step 4 ruled that Jews forcing unlawfully makes the גט פסול ופוסל.

phrases.english: and let it also disqualify her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רב משרשיא's claim that by Torah law a gentile-forced גט is כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If gentile force equals Jewish force by Torah law, unlawful gentile force should equal unlawful Jewish force and be פסול ופוסל, not 'no smell of a גט'.

steps.title: רב משרשיא's statement is rejected as a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב משרשיא's statement is a mistake and cannot be relied on.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, that statement of רב משרשיא is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא throws out רב משרשיא's answer because it cannot fit with שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the challenge in step 8 has no answer, רב משרשיא's idea that a gentile-forced גט is כשר by Torah law is rejected completely. That brings back the question from step 6, and the next step gives a new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake; a made-up idea with no basis

steps.whatToRemember: A גט forced by gentiles is not valid by Torah law; רב משרשיא's claim that it is was rejected as a mistake.

phrases.english: Rather, that statement of רב משרשיא
is a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בְּדוּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 8 and rejects step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire statement of רב משרשיא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts שמואל's ruling that an unlawful gentile-forced גט has no effect at all
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב משרשיא's statement is rejected; a gentile-forced גט is not כשר by Torah law.

steps.title: The real reason: lawful gentile force can be confused with lawful Jewish force
steps.stepSummary: A lawful gentile-forced גט is פסול ופוסל because people could confuse it with a lawful Jewish-forced גט. An unlawful gentile-forced גט cannot be confused with it, so it is not a גט at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason? A lawful forcing by gentiles can be confused with a lawful forcing by Jews. An unlawful forcing by gentiles cannot be confused with a lawful forcing by Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא's explanation was just rejected, so the גמרא gives a new reason for שמואל's two rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lawful gentile-forced גט looks a lot like a lawful Jewish-forced גט, which is valid. If we treated the gentile one as nothing, people might treat the Jewish one as nothing too, so the רבנן made it פוסל. An unlawful gentile forcing looks nothing like a proper Jewish court case, so there is no worry, and it stays completely empty.

keyTerms.meaning: Lawfully, according to the הלכה (the husband really was obligated to divorce)
Unlawfully, with no real obligation in הלכה to divorce
Can be mixed up or confused with
Reason

steps.confusionAlert: This new reason is not the same as רב משרשיא's rejected one. He said gentile force is valid by Torah law. Here the point is that the gentile-forced גט is פוסל only so people do not confuse it with a lawful Jewish-forced גט.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why did שמואל make a lawful gentile-forced גט פסול ופוסל but an unlawful one nothing at all?

phrases.english: Lawful forcing [by gentiles] can be confused with lawful forcing by Jews.
Unlawful forcing [by gentiles] cannot be confused with lawful forcing by Jews.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רב משרשיא in step 9, the גמרא gives a new explanation for שמואל's ruling in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic decree based on fear of confusion (גזירה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Gentile force must either count fully or not at all, so a split ruling makes no sense (step 6).
steps.terutzMaskana: The split ruling comes from how much each case looks like a lawful Jewish-forced גט. The look-alike case is made פוסל, and the case that does not look alike is left as nothing.

steps.title: אביי challenges רב יוסף for forcing a גט without being ordained
steps.stepSummary: אביי sees רב יוסף forcing husbands to give a גט. He asks how they can do this when they are not ordained judges, since רבי טרפון learns that cases may be judged only before ordained judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי found רב יוסף sitting and forcing husbands to give a גט. He said to him: But we are not ordained judges! And it was taught that רבי טרפון said: Anywhere you find gentile courts, even if their laws are like Jewish laws, you may not go to them, as it says, 'These are the laws that you shall set before them.' 'Before them' means not before gentiles. Another explanation: 'before them' means not before unordained judges.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins: אביי questions רב יוסף's right to force husbands to divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forcing a גט is a real court act, so it needs real judges. The פסוק 'לפניהם' teaches that court cases must come before proper judges, which excludes gentiles and also excludes הדיוטות (unordained judges). Since the judges in בבל have no סמיכה, אביי asks how רב יוסף can force anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Forcing husbands to give a גט
Here: judges without סמיכה (not ordained)
Gentile courts
To go to them, to use them for judgment
Another explanation

steps.confusionAlert: הדיוטות here does not mean ignorant people. רב יוסף and אביי were great scholars. It means judges who lack the formal סמיכה from ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: אביי found רב יוסף
sitting and forcing husbands to give bills of divorce.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא אֲנַן – הֶדְיוֹטוֹת אֲנַן,
phrases.english: He said to him: But we are ordinary people (not ordained),
and it was taught: רבי טרפון would say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֲגוֹרִיאוֹת שֶׁל גּוֹיִם,
phrases.english: Any place where you find courts of gentiles,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדִּינֵיהֶם כְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל –
phrases.english: even though their laws are like Jewish laws,
you are not permitted to go to them,
as it says: 'And these are the laws that you shall set before them';
'before them' and not before gentiles.
Another explanation: 'before them' and not before ordinary (unordained) people!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא אֲנַן – הֶדְיוֹטוֹת אֲנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from gentile-forced גט to the question of which Jewish judges may force a גט.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's practice of forcing husbands to give a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forcing a גט needs proper judges. The פסוק 'לפניהם' excludes הדיוטות, and the judges in בבל are not ordained, so they should have no power to force.

steps.title: רב יוסף: we act as agents of the ordained judges
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the judges of בבל act as שלוחים of the ordained judges of ארץ ישראל, just as they do when they judge admissions and loans.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We are carrying out their agency, just as we do with admissions and loans.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his practice by explaining where his authority comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judges in בבל do not judge on their own power. They act as the agents of the ordained judges, so it is as if those judges are acting. This is the same rule that already lets them judge everyday money cases like admissions and loans.

keyTerms.meaning: Their agency, acting on behalf of the ordained judges
We do, we carry out
Just like the case of
Admissions of debt and loans

phrases.english: He said to him: We
are carrying out their agency,
phrases.notes: 'Their' means the ordained judges of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: just as with admissions and loans.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Unordained judges have no court power at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: They have court power as agents of the ordained judges, as already seen in admissions and loans.

steps.title: Then why not judge robbery and injury cases too?
steps.stepSummary: If the judges of בבל act as agents, they should also be able to judge robbery and injury cases, which they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then robbery and injury cases too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's agency idea: it seems to prove too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is a known rule that judges outside ארץ ישראל do not rule on robbery and injury cases. If agency gives them the power of ordained judges, there should be no difference between these cases and loans.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Robbery cases
Cases of personal injury

phrases.english: If so, robbery and injury cases too!
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes the known rule that judges outside ארץ ישראל do not rule on robbery and injury cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the agency answer of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the judges of בבל act as agents of the ordained judges
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If agency works, it should work for every type of case. Yet robbery and injury are not judged outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The agency covers only common cases
steps.stepSummary: The agency of the ordained judges covers only common matters, not rare ones like robbery and injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we carry out their agency, it is in common matters. In uncommon matters, we do not carry out their agency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by setting a limit on the agency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ordained judges gave agency only for cases that come up often, like loans and admissions. Rare cases like robbery and injury were not included. That is why these cases are not judged outside ארץ ישראל, while the agency still holds for common matters.

keyTerms.meaning: A common matter, something that happens often
An uncommon, rare matter

steps.whatToRemember: Judges outside ארץ ישראל lack סמיכה but act as agents of the ordained judges. That agency covers common cases (like loans and admissions), and רב יוסף uses it to force a גט, but it does not cover rare cases like robbery and injury.

phrases.english: When we carry out their agency, it is in a common matter;

phrases.aramaic: בְּמִילְּתָא דְּלָא שְׁכִיחָא – לָא עָבְדִינַן שְׁלִיחוּתַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: in an uncommon matter, we do not carry out their agency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by limiting the agency of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule (common vs. uncommon cases)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Agency gives the judges of בבל full power in every kind of case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Agency covers only common matters, so robbery and injury cases are excluded.

steps.title: A rumor in town can make a woman betrothed or divorced
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a rumor that a woman is מקודשת makes her betrothed. A rumor that she is מגורשת makes her divorced, as long as there is no אמתלא.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a rumor spread in the city that a woman is betrothed, she is treated as betrothed. If the rumor is that she is divorced, she is treated as divorced. This applies only if there is no explanation that weakens the rumor.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a strong public rumor about a woman's marital status is taken seriously, unless there is an אמתלא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we need witnesses to establish קידושין or גירושין. Here the משנה says a widespread rumor (קלא) is enough to set her status. The exception is when there is an אמתלא, a reason that makes the rumor less meaningful.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A rumor about her went out in the city
Betrothed (has קידושין)
Divorced (received a גט)
An excuse or explanation that weakens the rumor

phrases.english: MISHNA
If a rumor went out in the city that she is "betrothed"
she is betrothed;
if the rumor is "divorced," she is divorced.
provided there is no explanation there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, separate from the earlier discussion of a forced גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A town rumor of קידושין or גירושין sets the woman's status, unless there is an אמתלא.

steps.title: Examples of an explanation that weakens the rumor
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines אמתלא with two examples. One is a rumor of a גט given on a condition. The other is a rumor of קידושין thrown to her where it is unclear whether they landed closer to her or to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What counts as an explanation? For example, people also say that so-and-so divorced his wife on a condition. Or he threw her betrothal money to her, and it is unclear whether it landed closer to her or closer to him. That is an explanation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains its own word אמתלא by giving concrete examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both examples the rumor itself carries a detail showing that the event might not have actually worked. A conditional גט may never take effect if the condition is not met. Thrown קידושין work only if they landed closer to her, so a doubt about where they landed leaves the קידושין in doubt. Because of this, the rumor does not prove anything.

keyTerms.meaning: On a condition
He threw her betrothal money or object to her

keyTerms.term: סָפֵק קָרוֹב לָהּ סָפֵק קָרוֹב לוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: Unclear whether it landed closer to her or closer to him

phrases.english: What is an explanation?

phrases.aramaic: גֵּירַשׁ אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ עַל תְּנַאי;
phrases.english: So-and-so divorced his wife on a condition;
or he threw her betrothal to her,

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק קָרוֹב לָהּ, סָפֵק קָרוֹב לוֹ –
phrases.english: and it is unclear whether it was closer to her or closer to him,
this is an explanation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term אמתלא used in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A conditional גט or doubtful thrown קידושין count as an אמתלא, so the rumor does not decide her status.

steps.title: Can a rumor separate a married woman from her husband?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that a rumor of divorce counts. רב אשי said we ignore any rumor that comes after נישואין, so how can a rumor forbid a married woman to her husband?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Would we really forbid her to her husband because of a rumor? But רב אשי said: any rumor that comes after marriage, we are not concerned about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second half of the משנה, the part about a rumor that she is מגורשת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seemed to say a rumor of divorce makes her divorced, even if she is living with her husband. רב אשי's rule says a rumor that starts after the couple is already fully married carries no weight. So the משנה seems to contradict רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
We forbid her to her husband
A rumor or public talk
Full marriage, after the חופה
We are not concerned about it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse קידושין (betrothal) with נישואין (full marriage). רב אשי's rule is only about rumors that start after נישואין.

phrases.english: GEMARA
And do we forbid her to her husband?!
But didn't רב אשי say:
any rumor that comes after marriage,
we are not concerned about it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָסְרִינַן לַהּ אַגַּבְרָא וְהָא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a rumor of divorce makes a woman divorced
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב אשי says a rumor after נישואין is ignored, so a rumor should not be able to separate a married woman from her husband.

steps.title: Rereading the משנה as a rumor of betrothal and then divorce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets the משנה. 'Divorced' refers to a rumor that she was betrothed and then divorced, not to a rumor about a married woman. The explanation continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה is saying: if a rumor spread in the city that she is betrothed, she is betrothed. If the rumor is that she is betrothed and divorced...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the משנה really means. It begins rereading the משנה, and the sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the משנה is not talking about a rumor that starts after נישואין, so רב אשי's rule is not contradicted. The 'divorced' case becomes one where people said she was both מקודשת and then מגורשת. The ruling for that case comes in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of the source)
Betrothed and then divorced

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
If a rumor went out in the city that she is "betrothed"
she is betrothed.
If the rumor is "betrothed and divorced"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17 by reinterpreting the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'מגורשת' meant a rumor that a married woman was divorced.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's 'מגורשת' refers to a rumor that she was betrothed and then divorced, so רב אשי's rule about rumors after נישואין does not apply.
